chunks: Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abu al-Mi'za from Abu Basir said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-hibah (gift) is valid whether it has been taken possession of or not, divided or not divided. And an-nuhlah (gift given for a specific purpose/reason) is not valid until it is taken possession of, and the people intended that but were mistaken.'

key_terms.اَلنُّحْلُ: Gift given for a specific reason or condition

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between hibah and nuhlah in Shia fiqh regarding possession?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies a legal nuance in gift-giving by distinguishing between 'al-hibah' (a general gift, valid upon declaration regardless of possession) and 'an-nuhlah' (a specific gift, requiring actual possession). He notes that while people commonly assumed possession was required for all gifts, this was a misconception; the validity of 'hibah' is established by the contract itself, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intention and declaration in civil transactions.
